To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the lower bound on the entanglements of formation of arbitrary mixed Gaussian states is the entanglement that would be obtained if the Gaussian state was replaced by a squeezed state with equal entanglement of purification; and (ii) this lower bound is equal to the logarithmic negativity of the Gaussian state, and thus it is a lower bound on the logarithmic negativity as well.

(1) the entanglement per particle of a Gaussian state is bounded by a function of the symplectic spectrum, and (2) for any mixed Gaussian state the entanglement is bounded by a linear combination of its symplectic eigenvalues.

(i) the entanglement per mode of a general two-mode Gaussian state can be lower-bounded by 2.5 log2(1+2v) − 2.5, where v is the symmetrized variance of the state, and (ii) the entanglements of formation of two-mode Gaussian states are lower bounded by the entanglement entropies of the corresponding two-mode squeezed vacuum states.
